- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly, especially after sharp spikes.
- When sentiment is negative (≤-0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast modestly, especially if recent price is trending up.
- Model frequently overshoots after strong upward sentiment spikes; apply a 5-10% downward correction to forecast 3-5 days post-spike.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model often lags; adjust forecast upward by 2-5% in the 10-15 day window.
- Mean reversion is common in 10-15 day windows; if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 2-5% unless sentiment strongly supports.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to be too optimistic when sentiment is high; apply a 3-7% downward bias if sentiment >0.75 over last 7 days.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is trending, model often misses the direction; align forecast with sentiment direction, not just history.
